question: A matrix $P$ has elements $p_{ij} = i - j$ for $1 \leq i,j \leq 3$. Find $P$, calculate $|P|$, and interpret whether the matrix is invertible.
explanation:
Step 1: Write matrix $P$:
For $i=1$: $j=1\to0, j=2\to-1, j=3\to-2$
$i=2$: $j=1\to1, j=2\to0, j=3\to-1$
$i=3$: $j=1\to2, j=2\to1, j=3\to0$
So $P=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$

Step 2: $|P| = 0 \begin{vmatrix}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} - (-1) \begin{vmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{vmatrix} + (-2) \begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{vmatrix}$

First minor: $0*0-1*(-1)=0+1=1$
Second: $1*0-(-1)*2=0+2=2$
Third: $1*1-0*2=1-0=1$

So $|P| = 0 - (-1)*2 + (-2)*1 = 0 + 2 -2 = 0$

Hence, $P$ is singular; it is not invertible.

options.A: $P=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1&-2\\1&0&-1\\2&1&0\end{bmatrix}$, $|P|=0$, so $P$ is singular and not invertible.
